Question 3 / Auscare Group

Better efficiency. Considered decisions.

Situation

Amazon ACOS was 42% across two FMCG brands. Spend was too high relative to attributed sales.

Task

Reduce advertising cost of sales while protecting the brands’ visibility.

Action

Reviewed weekly ROAS, ACOS, CTR and conversion data. Identified weak keywords, audiences and placements, then moved budget in stages and tested each change.

18–25%
Reported paid campaign CTR improvement

The judgement was knowing where to keep pushing efficiency and when a lower ACOS could reduce visibility.

ACOS = ad spend ÷ attributed advertising sales. Reported results; periods and analytics exports were not supplied.

Sources: original Enigma application and portfolio website, Auscare case study. Analysis covered Meta, Amazon and Google, using platform reports, SEMrush and GA4. The ACOS result is Amazon-specific; the CTR range is a paid-campaign result across the supplied portfolio and should not be read as an Amazon-only measurement. The original application also cites A$3.6M combined annual revenue for the brands, which is business context rather than incremental revenue attributable to this optimisation.

Question 2 / My media perspective

Three shifts I’m watching

The practical question is how each shift changes a planning or buying decision.

01

Retail media &
first-party data

Retail networks connect media with purchase-intent signals and shopping behaviour.

My focus: match the placement to intent and evaluate its commercial contribution.

02

Attention &
outcomes

Reach and clicks tell only part of the story. I want to understand what people notice and do next.

My focus: choose measures that reflect the campaign’s actual objective.

03

AI-assisted
buying

Automation supports bidding and optimisation, while judgement shapes the objective and constraints.

My focus: test recommendations and keep human responsibility for the decision.

Adapted from the original application’s media trends response. These are Jen’s areas of interest and practical planning priorities, rather than a quantified market forecast. Retail media is described without assuming a universal third-party-cookie phase-out.
Question 2 / Creative judgement

How I would evaluate AI-assisted creative

Give the work a fair test.
Keep the standard high.

I would assess the work against the brief and audience response. An AI label alone does not tell us whether it is effective.

Disclosure and quality checks help make that evaluation trustworthy.

01
Check the brief

Is the message relevant, accurate and consistent with the brand?

02
Test the response

Use comparable conditions and measures such as CTR, conversion or brand lift.

03
Review quality & disclosure

Check the claims and assets, decide what needs disclosure, and apply human approval.

04
Keep what the evidence supports

Refine or reject creative based on its quality and performance.

Proposed evaluation approach. This slide describes how I would assess creative, rather than claiming results from an AI campaign.

Based on the original application’s AI creative perspective. It argues against prejudging creative by how it was produced and for evaluation using performance, disclosure and quality assurance. No unsupported claim that AI creative outperforms human-produced work is made here.
